# requireNumber

<link-summary>Returns the value as a number, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireNumber() — Returns the value as a number, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireNumber(value: unknown, message: string = "Expected a number."): number;
```

The test is `typeof value === "number"`, which `NaN` and both infinities satisfy. Use `isFloat`, `isInteger` or `isNaN` when those cases have to be told apart.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                       | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :---------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                         | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a number."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number` — the same value, typed as a number.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                  |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------- |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a number. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireNumber(0); // => 0
requireNumber(1.5); // => 1.5
requireNumber("1"); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNumber(null); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
